content.value_statement: Teams often overcommit because milestones and capacity are not planned together. This skill helps you turn goals into sized epics, sprint allocations, and clear roadmap decisions.
actual_capabilities: Defines a quarterly roadmap using a six-sprint planning horizon.
Breaks strategic epics into two to four capacity-sized milestones.
Applies the documented point, duration, and capacity model.
Allocates milestones to two-week sprints with a recommended buffer.
Guides collaborative planning questions for quarters, epics, and sprints.
Explains the documented mapping between roadmap items and ClickUp tasks.
limitations: It provides planning guidance and does not create detailed specifications or QA plans.
Estimates use a simple point model and require team validation.
ClickUp synchronization depends on separate ClickUp commands being available.
It does not replace current delivery data, stakeholder decisions, or project management judgment.

use_cases.title: Create a quarterly roadmap
use_cases.description: Turn product goals into a sequenced set of epics and milestones for the next six sprints.

use_cases.title: Balance sprint capacity
use_cases.description: Allocate planned milestones to a two-week sprint while retaining buffer for unexpected work.

use_cases.title: Prepare an epic delivery plan
use_cases.description: Split a large initiative into meaningful milestones that can be estimated and tracked.

prompt_templates.title: Start a roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a quarterly roadmap for a team of 4 developers. Our goals are faster onboarding and improved reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Break down an epic
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this epic into 2 to 4 milestones: add team-based permissions to our application. Suggest point estimates and dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a sprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the next two-week sprint for 3 developers. We have 48 points of effective capacity after a 15% buffer. These are the available milestones: [list].

prompt_templates.title: Review a constrained roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this six-sprint roadmap for capacity conflicts, oversized milestones, and sequencing risks. Propose a revised allocation and explain each change: [roadmap].

output_examples.input: Plan a quarter for a four-developer team with onboarding and reporting goals.
output: A six-sprint sequence of prioritized epics.
Milestones with point estimates and owners to confirm.
A capacity check that includes a 15% buffer.

output_examples.input: Split an 30-point permissions epic into milestones.
output: Identity model and role definitions: 10 points.
Permission enforcement in core workflows: 12 points.

best_practices: Confirm goals, constraints, and team availability before estimating work.
Split milestones that exceed 25 points before assigning them to a sprint.
Review the roadmap with stakeholders and adjust it as delivery information changes.
anti_patterns: Treating point estimates as guaranteed delivery dates.
Filling every sprint to full nominal capacity without a buffer.
Using roadmap milestones as replacements for detailed engineering specifications.

faq.question: What sprint length does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses a two-week sprint with 10 working days.

faq.question: How much capacity is one developer?
faq.answer: The documented model uses 20 points per developer for a two-week sprint.

faq.question: How large should a milestone be?
faq.answer: Milestones should be meaningful checkpoints and should be split when they exceed 25 points.

faq.question: Does the skill create detailed specifications?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on strategic planning rather than detailed specifications, PR tracking, or QA.

faq.question: Should every sprint be fully allocated?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends a 15% buffer for unexpected work.

faq.question: Can I synchronize the roadmap with ClickUp?
faq.answer: The documentation describes separate ClickUp push and pull commands for epics and milestones.
